title: Welcome to our newest members
excerpt: Eleven businesses joined this month, from a bakery to a bike shop. Here's who they are and how to say hello.
content:
Eleven businesses joined the chamber this month. Please say hello at the next breakfast, and give them a try.

Opening their doors

Okafor Bakeries opened its third shop on Elm Street, Prairie Outfitters moved into the old shoe shop on Lake Drive, and Still Water Yoga started evening classes on Lawrence Avenue.

New to the chamber

Ruiz Accounting, Move Well Physio, Capital HR, Lakeside Kayaks, Harbor Storage, Second Act, Oakline Joinery and Literacy Springfield have all joined too. You'll find every one of them in the member directory.

Thinking of joining? Membership starts at $60 a year, and your first breakfast is on us. Apply in five minutes.

title: Five ways to get more from your directory listing
excerpt: A good photo, one clear line and a working phone number do most of the work. Here's what the busiest listings have in common.
content:
Your listing in the member directory is seen by people looking for a local business right now. These five things make the most difference.

1. Use a real photo

A photo of your shop front, your team or your work. People pick the listing that looks like a real place.

2. Say what you do in one line

"Family dentistry with evening appointments" beats a paragraph. Say who it's for and what makes you different.

3. Check your phone number and hours

The most common complaint we hear is a number that doesn't answer. Check yours every few months.

4. Offer a member deal

Listings with a member deal get far more clicks. It can be small: ten percent, or a free coffee.

5. Tell us when things change

New hours, a new shop or a new phone number? Email the office and we'll update it the same week.

title: What the new downtown parking plan means for you
excerpt: Two hours free on Main Street, new spaces behind the library and no change to permits. Here's what members asked for and what the council agreed.
content:
Last month the city council voted on the new downtown parking plan. Nearly two hundred members answered our survey, and the plan that passed is very different from the first draft.

What changes

The first two hours on Main Street and Adams Street are now free, up from one. Forty new spaces open behind the library in June. Meters take cards and phones from April.

What stays the same

Staff permits keep their price for two more years, and loading bays stay where they are.

What we asked for and didn't get

We asked for free parking after 6pm. The council will look at it again next year, and we'll keep asking.

Questions about how it affects your business? Get in touch, or come to the next board meeting.

title: Hiring your first employee: notes from the breakfast
excerpt: Payroll, contracts and the one mistake almost everyone makes. The notes from this month's business breakfast.
content:
Forty-two members came to this month's breakfast to hear Lena Ruiz of Ruiz Accounting talk about taking on a first employee. Here are the main points.

Before you hire

Work out the full cost, not just the wage: payroll taxes, insurance and time off add about a fifth. Register as an employer before the first payday.

The paperwork

Every new hire needs a written offer, the right forms for tax and right to work, and a simple handbook. Capital HR has a free template for members.

The mistake almost everyone makes

Hiring someone just like you. Hire for the jobs you're worst at or least like doing.

Missed it? The slides are on the members' page, and the next breakfast is on the second Thursday.
